elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60–90 days' notice
elements.evidence: a. providing at least one month's prior written notice to IBM (roughly 30 days, shorter than the 60–90 day fallback band, though favourable to Customer)

elements.element: Early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees
elements.evidence: provided that such early termination charges will not in the aggregate exceed three (3) months' Charges for the terminated Services

elements.element: Vendor convenience termination permitted only effective at the end of a term
elements.evidence: No operative language in the redlined clause or supplied excerpt addresses any IBM termination-for-convenience right

elements.element: Vendor end-of-term convenience termination requires 90 days' notice
elements.evidence: No notice requirement is imposed on IBM anywhere in the edited text

elements.element: Customer termination for convenience on 30 days' written notice (preferred)
elements.evidence: terminate ... for convenience at the end of any calendar month by: a. providing at least one month's prior written notice
IBM will refund to Customer, within thirty (30) days ... any Charges prepaid by Customer for Services attributable to the period after that date

elements.element: No Vendor termination-for-convenience right during a committed term (preferred)
elements.evidence: The redline is silent on IBM's convenience termination rights; no prohibition was inserted

offending_extra_words: IBM will refund to Customer, within thirty (30) days after the effective date of such termination, any Charges prepaid by Customer for Services attributable to the period after that date.
provided that such early termination charges will not in the aggregate exceed three (3) months' Charges for the terminated Services
reasons: The drafter locked to fallback, but the inserted pro-rata prepaid-fee refund is a preferred-level element; mixing a preferred remedy into a fallback edit fails minimality without completing either bargain.

The fallback's Vendor-side constraints (convenience termination only effective at the end of the then-current term, on 90 days' notice) are not expressed anywhere in the edit, so the fallback level is incomplete.

Operation 1 rewrites limb (b) at more than twice its original length; the cap could be added as a short proviso or a separate one-sentence insertion (e.g. 'Early termination charges will not exceed three (3) months' Charges.').
Customer's one month's notice is shorter than the 60–90 day fallback band but is favourable to us, so it should be noted in the rationale rather than redlined.
No undefined terms or dangling mechanics are introduced; 'Charges' and 'Services' track the Agreement's defined usage, so intent is preserved.
